currency.name: Ethereum

priceApi._comment: Price APIs are tried in order: CoinGecko → CMC → Coinpaprika → DEX

cmc._comment: Requires CMC_API_KEY environment variable. ID is the CMC slug.

dex._comment: On-chain price from the wrapped native / stablecoin pool, used when no API above gives a price (disable the APIs to make it the only source). Needs dex.wrappedNative. pairAddress and stablecoinAddress are optional: left out or zero, the pool is looked up among dex.lpTokens / dex.farmPools and the stablecoin is dex.tokens.usdt. Decimals are read from the token contracts.

currency._comment: For custom networks: name/symbol/unit/gasUnit can be customized (e.g., VirBiCoin/VBC/niku/Gniku)

addressTags._comment: Public name tags shown next to addresses (Etherscan-style). DEX/Launchpad/Bridge/miners addresses are tagged automatically from their own config sections; entries here add to or override those.

explorer.name: Blockchain Explorer
explorer.description: Real-time blockchain explorer for EVM-compatible networks

network.name: Ethereum Mainnet
network._comment: slug is used for URL-friendly identifiers (e.g., virbicoin for VirBiCoin network)

dex._comment: The factory, wrapped native token, reward token, tokens, pairs (lpTokens) and farms (farmPools) are read from the router and MasterChef. Write any of them here to use your own value instead of the chain's (a written list is the whole list).

autoSwap._comment: Optional: lock-and-swap entry contract on this chain. When set (and 'swap' below is configured), the deposit form offers receiving remote assets (e.g. BNB/USDT) directly in one transaction.

swap._comment: Optional in-page swap: 'router' is a Uniswap V2-style router on the remote chain, 'wrappedNative' its wrapped native token (routing hop), 'outputs' the assets the wrapped token can be converted into (kind 'native', or 'erc20' with address/decimals).

bridge._comment: Cross-chain lock-and-mint bridge. 'routes' is a list, so more assets/destinations can be added over time. Per route: 'asset' is what leaves this chain (kind 'native', or 'erc20' with a 'token' address and 'decimals'); it is locked in 'vault' and minted as 'wrappedToken' on the remote chain. Optional 'dexName'/'swapUrl' link the wrapped token to an external DEX; optional 'swap' enables the in-page conversion widget. The legacy single 'vault'+'remote' shape (without 'routes') is still supported.

legacyFactories.note: Previous factory contract (optional, for showing tokens from old contracts)

alternativePayment._comment: Alternative payment token for token creation (e.g., project governance token). contractFunctions maps generic names to actual contract function names.

launchpad._comment: Token Launchpad for no-code token creation. Set factoryAddress to enable.

tokenIcons._comment: Token icons and gradient colors for UI display. Keys are token symbols.

contracts.name: Example Deprecated Contract
contracts.reason: Broken/superseded deployment; hidden from the contracts list (address page stays reachable)

launchpadTokens.reason: Test token, fully burned or deprecated

blacklist._comment: Blacklisted tokens/pairs will be hidden from DEX, Launchpad, and token lists

social._comment: Social media links displayed in footer and pages

dexInfo.name: Your DEX Name
dexInfo._comment: DEX metadata for GeckoTerminal/CoinGecko listing applications. Optional defillamaSlug: the DefiLlama protocol whose TVL /api/dex/external-price reports (api.llama.fi/tvl/<slug>); without it no TVL is fetched.

supply._comment: Supply calculation for /api/total_supply and /api/circulating_supply endpoints (CoinGecko/CMC compatible)

rewards._comment: Block reward schedule used for the supply endpoints, mining rewards and the reward countdown. blockReward: reward in coins (or 0x wei) keyed by the first block it applies to, like an OpenEthereum chainspec's blockReward. flatUncleRewardFrom: block from which uncles earn a flat 1/32 of the block reward (Ethereum Classic ECIP-1017: 5000001). forkNames: optional names for the blocks where the reward changes. Without this section the explorer uses Ethereum's schedule shown here.
